title: AI CBSE Class 10 | Revisiting Ai project cycle and ethics frameworks for ai
description: AI CBSE Class 10 | Revisiting Ai project cycle and ethics frameworks for ai
chapters: Revisiting Ai project cycle and ethics frameworks for ai
subject: ai-artificial-intelligence

questions.question: Which stage of the AI Project Cycle involves defining the goals and parameters of the problem?
questions.explanation: Problem Scoping is the initial stage where we identify the problem and define the boundaries of the project using the 4Ws canvas.
questions.hint: It's the "What, Who, Where, Why" stage.

questions.question: In the 4Ws Problem Canvas, 'Who' refers to:

options.text: The people developing the AI model.
The stakeholders who are facing the problem.
The hardware used for the AI.
The location where the problem occurs.

questions.explanation: The 'Who' block helps identify the people or groups directly affected by the problem.
questions.hint: Think about the "target audience" or victims of the issue.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of 'Secondary Data'?

options.text: Data collected through a personal interview.
Data recorded during a live experiment.
Data downloaded from a government website or Kaggle.
Data gathered via a customized survey.

questions.explanation: Secondary data is information that already exists and was collected by someone else for a different purpose.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of 'Data Exploration'?

options.text: To delete all data from the database.
To understand the patterns and trends within the collected data.
To write the final code for the AI.
To present the final product to the client.

questions.explanation: Data Exploration helps visualize the data to find anomalies, patterns, and correlations before modelling.
questions.hint: It's about "seeing" what the data tells us.

questions.question: A rule-based AI model is different from a learning-based model because:

options.text: It works on pre-defined logic provided by the developer.
It learns from experience and data patterns.
It can handle unpredictable data automatically.
It requires no human intervention at all.

questions.explanation: Rule-based models follow specific "If-Then" rules coded by humans, whereas learning-based models find their own patterns.
questions.hint: Think of it as "Static" vs "Dynamic" logic.

questions.question: Which AI domain is primarily used in self-driving cars to detect pedestrians?
questions.explanation: Computer Vision allows machines to interpret and understand the visual world (images and videos).

questions.question: Which domain of AI is used when you interact with a chatbot like Alexa or Siri?
questions.explanation: NLP deals with the interaction between computers and human languages.
questions.hint: It's about communication through text or speech.

questions.question: When an AI model shows a preference for one group over another due to faulty training data, it is called:
questions.explanation: Bias occurs when the input data is not representative, leading to unfair outcomes for certain groups.
questions.hint: It is a "prejudice" in the system.

questions.question: Which ethical framework principle ensures that AI systems are understandable to humans?
questions.explanation: Transparency means the logic and decisions made by the AI should be explainable and open to inspection.
questions.hint: It's the opposite of a "Black Box" system.

questions.question: Exploring Bioethics in AI primarily deals with:

options.text: How fast an AI can process biological data.
The ethical implications of AI on human biology, healthcare, and life.
Using AI to grow plants in a lab.

questions.explanation: Bioethics examines the moral issues arising from advances in biology and medicine, especially when integrated with AI.

questions.question: In the 'Statement of Purpose' (SoP), which element describes the final outcome or benefit?
questions.explanation: The 'Why' part of the SoP focuses on the value the solution provides to the stakeholders.
questions.hint: It answers "What's the point of doing this?"

questions.question: Which of these is a 'HOTS' scenario: If an AI used for medical diagnosis is trained only on data from one city, what is the most likely risk?

options.text: The AI will run out of memory.
The AI will not be accurate for patients from other geographical regions.
The AI will become a robot.
The AI will stop working after two days.

questions.explanation: This is an example of data bias/lack of diversity, making the model non-generalizable.

questions.question: What happens in the 'Modelling' stage of the AI Project Cycle?

options.text: An algorithm is chosen and trained on the data.

questions.explanation: Modelling is where the actual AI model is built and trained using algorithms.
questions.hint: This is where the "intelligence" is created.

questions.question: 'System Maps' are used in which phase of the project cycle to understand relationships between elements?
questions.explanation: System maps help visualize complex relationships and loops within the problem environment during scoping.

questions.question: Which of the following is a concern regarding AI and 'Job Displacement'?

options.text: Automation might replace human workers in repetitive tasks.
Humans will have to work 24 hours a day.
AI cannot do any human tasks.

questions.explanation: One of the major social concerns is that AI automation may lead to unemployment in certain sectors.

questions.question: The concept of 'Data Privacy' ensures that:

options.text: Personal data is handled securely and with consent.
Only AI models can see the data.

questions.explanation: Privacy is the right of individuals to control how their personal information is collected and used.

questions.question: Which of these AI domains would be most useful for predicting stock market trends based on 20 years of numbers?
questions.explanation: Data Science is the domain used to analyze and interpret large volumes of numerical and structured data.

questions.question: 'Reliability' of data acquisition means:

options.text: The data comes from a trusted and accurate source.
The data is in a colorful format.

questions.explanation: Reliable data ensures that the AI model is built on facts rather than errors.

questions.question: In the context of Ethics, 'Accountability' means:

options.text: Identifying who is responsible for the AI's actions and decisions.
Keeping a count of the data points.

questions.explanation: Accountability ensures there is a human or entity responsible if the AI causes harm.
questions.hint: It answers the question "Who is to blame if something goes wrong?"

questions.question: A 'Neural Link' between a brain and a computer is a topic studied under:
questions.explanation: Connecting technology directly to the human brain raises deep ethical questions about identity and control.

questions.question: Which part of the 4Ws canvas explores the 'Nature' of the problem?
questions.explanation: The 'What' block helps in clearly defining what the problem is and what evidence we have for it.

questions.question: What is the final step of the AI Project Cycle?
questions.explanation: Evaluation is the final phase where the model's performance is tested against real-world metrics.

questions.question: Which AI concern deals with the 'Digital Divide'?

options.text: Inequality in access to AI technology.
AI becoming too smart for humans.
The cost of electricity to run AI.
The size of the AI hardware.

questions.explanation: The digital divide refers to the gap between those who have access to AI benefits and those who do not.

questions.question: If an AI classifies an email as 'Spam' when it is actually 'Important', this is an error in:
questions.explanation: This is a classification error (False Positive) which is identified during the evaluation phase.

questions.question: Using AI to edit human genes is a concern of:
questions.explanation: Gene editing (CRISPR, etc.) combined with AI for selection raises massive ethical concerns about "designer babies."

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a component of the AI Project Cycle?
questions.explanation: The project cycle focuses on the software/logical development of the AI, not the physical factory manufacturing.

questions.question: 'Fairness' in AI frameworks means:

options.text: Ensuring the AI does not discriminate against any group.
Making the AI free for everyone.
Ensuring the AI works very fast.

questions.explanation: Fairness involves actively preventing bias to ensure equitable treatment for all users.

questions.question: Sentiment Analysis (finding if a review is happy or sad) belongs to:
questions.explanation: Analyzing the emotion behind human text is a core task of Natural Language Processing.

questions.question: 'Big Data' is a core foundation for which domain?
questions.explanation: Data Science thrives on large datasets to find hidden correlations.

questions.question: Why is 'Consent' important in AI?

options.text: It makes the code run faster.
It ensures users agree to how their data is used.
It is required to buy the hardware.
It helps in naming the AI.

questions.explanation: Consent is a legal and ethical requirement to respect user privacy and autonomy.

questions.question: Which of the following are part of the 4Ws Problem Canvas? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: The 4Ws are Who, What, Where, and Why. 'When' is not a standard part of this specific canvas.

questions.question: Identify the sources of Data Acquisition. (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Sensors, surveys, and web scraping are methods to get data. Scoping is a phase, not a source.

questions.question: Which of these are domains of Artificial Intelligence? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: The three main domains we study in Class 10 AI are Data, CV, and NLP.

questions.question: What are the common issues and concerns related to AI? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Privacy, Bias, and Job loss are major concerns. AI usually decreases manual labor through automation.

questions.question: Ethical frameworks for AI often include which of the following? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: All four are core pillars of responsible AI development.

questions.question: Which of the following are examples of Computer Vision application? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Face recognition, X-rays, and QR codes involve visual data. Spam filters use NLP/Text.

questions.question: Which of these are tasks performed in Natural Language Processing? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Translation, speech conversion, and summarization involve human language. House prices involve numerical data (Data Science).

questions.question: Bioethics in AI covers which of the following topics? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Bioethics focuses on healthcare, the human body, and biological data. UI/UX (colors) is not bioethics.

questions.question: In Data Exploration, which visuals are commonly used? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Charts and plots help visualize patterns. Code is the tool, not the visualization itself.

questions.question: Which of these are characteristics of a 'Learning-based' model? (Select all that apply)

options.text: It follows a fixed set of If-Then rules.
It is used in unpredictable environments.

questions.explanation: Learning models are dynamic and data-driven. Rule-based models follow fixed logic.

questions.question: Why is 'Diverse Data' important during Data Acquisition? (Select all that apply)

options.text: To make the model more accurate for everyone.
To increase the price of the AI.

questions.explanation: Diversity ensures the AI works for everyone, not just a specific group, and prevents bias.

questions.question: Stakeholders in an AI project could include: (Select all that apply)

options.text: The people affected by the problem.

questions.explanation: Stakeholders are people or organizations with an interest or "stake" in the project.

questions.question: Which of the following describe 'What' in the 4Ws canvas? (Select all that apply)

options.text: The evidence that a problem exists.
The specific nature of the problem.

questions.explanation: 'What' covers the problem description and evidence. Location is 'Where', people are 'Who'.

questions.question: Which of these are 'NLP' based applications? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Translate, Autocorrect, and Voice assistants process language. Navigation is primarily CV.

questions.question: Challenges in Bioethics include: (Select all that apply)

options.text: Loss of human agency in medical decisions.
Inequality in access to life-saving AI.

questions.explanation: Healthcare bias, losing control over medical choices, and unfair access are ethical bio-challenges.

questions.question: What constitutes 'Good Quality Data'? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Accurate, relevant, and complete data ensures a reliable model.

questions.question: 'Transparency' in AI implies: (Select all that apply)

options.text: Users know when they are interacting with an AI.
The decision-making process can be explained.
The AI uses transparent plastic hardware.
Openness about what data is being used.

questions.explanation: It's about being "clear" and "explainable" in operations and data usage.

questions.question: AI Bias can enter a system through: (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Bias comes from human prejudice in data, logic, or limited testing environments.

questions.question: 'Data Science' can be used for: (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Weather, banking, and recommendations use huge datasets and stats. Handwriting is Computer Vision.

questions.question: The 'Where' block in Problem Scoping covers: (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: 'Where' defines the setting or environment. Stakeholders are 'Who', Reason is 'Why'.
